findings.evidence: `Complex.lean:52` `theorem inner_real_eq_re_inner (𝕜 ...) [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]`. Its docstring says it applies 'simultaneously to `InnerProductSpace.rclikeToReal` ... and to spaces such as `EuclideanSpace ℂ ι`'. It is already used this way in `Orthonormal/Complex.lean:96,113`.
findings.fix: Move it to `TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Complex.lean` as `theorem im_inner_eq_real_inner_I_smul {E} [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] (x y : E) : (⟪x, y⟫_ℂ).im = ⟪Complex.I • x, y⟫_ℝ`, proved via `inner_real_eq_re_inner ℂ, inner_smul_left`. The call sites in `Reduction/Hopf.lean` and `ComplexProjectiveSpace/Symplectic.lean` then use it unchanged.
findings.issue: `EuclideanSpace.im_inner_eq_real_inner_I_smul` is limited to `EuclideanSpace ℂ ι`, but its proof only uses `EuclideanSpace.real_inner_eq_re_inner`. That is the Euclidean case of `TauCeti.inner_real_eq_re_inner ℂ`, which holds on any `E` with `[InnerProductSpace ℂ E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]`.

findings.evidence: Both proofs at `Complex.lean:63-64` and `Complex.lean:70-71` start with the same rewrite chain: `inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right, ← mul_assoc, (RCLike|Complex).conj_mul`.
findings.fix: Add `inner_smul_smul {𝕜 E} [RCLike 𝕜] [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] (ζ : 𝕜) (x y : E) : ⟪ζ • x, ζ • y⟫_𝕜 = (‖ζ‖ : 𝕜) ^ 2 * ⟪x, y⟫_𝕜`. Derive `inner_smul_smul_circle` from it with `Circle.norm_coe`, and derive `real_inner_smul_smul` by taking real parts.
findings.issue: `inner_smul_smul_circle` is the `‖u‖ = 1` case of the general `⟪ζ • x, ζ • y⟫_𝕜 = ‖ζ‖ ^ 2 * ⟪x, y⟫_𝕜`. The neighbouring `real_inner_smul_smul` repeats the same `inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right, conj_mul` computation.

summary: `EuclideanSpace.im_inner_eq_real_inner_I_smul` is stated only for `EuclideanSpace ℂ ι`, although the `InnerProductSpace/Complex.lean` setup already gives it on any space with compatible complex and real inner products. The circle lemma is also the unit-norm case of a general `‖ζ‖ ^ 2` scaling formula.
